text: answer[math-5248264f-open]: The 8-queens problem has 92 distinct solutions when rotations and reflections are counted as distinct. This is the standard count for the classical problem on an 8×8 board. Each solution places 8 queens such that no two share the same row, column, or diagonal. The number 92 is well-established and refers to all fundamental and symmetric variations treated separately. Conversely, if you consider only the fundamental solutions (unique up to rotations and reflections), that count would be 12. Since the task specifies counting reflections and rotations as distinct, the correct answer is 92.
